whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls

items.title: California's Statute of Limitations Runs Fast
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim, but claims against a government entity (like a road defect on a city-maintained street) may require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can close the door on your case entirely.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Recovery
items.desc: California is a pure comparative fault state, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're partly at fault for the collision, though your award is reduced by your share of fault. We can help make sure fault isn't unfairly pinned on you before you've had a chance to tell your side.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: California places no cap on compensation for pain, suffering, and other non-economic losses in a standard car accident case. That's one more reason not to accept a quick settlement offer before understanding the full scope of your injuries.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. We can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my accident happened on Hawthorne Boulevard or another busy Rancho Palos Verdes corridor?
items.answer: High-traffic roads like Hawthorne Boulevard, Western Avenue, and Palos Verdes Drive S see a steady share of the city's reported injury collisions. Documenting the scene, getting a police report number, and seeking medical care quickly all help build a stronger record regardless of where the crash happened.

items.question: How much does it cost to contact an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer a free consultation, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront fee to speak with us about your Rancho Palos Verdes car accident.
